decisions.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): under_attack counted every drop reason, including drops storm mode itself causes, so legitimate fragmented or unparsable traffic could keep nodes under attack and the latch from ever seeing calm (ADR-0006: a cost bounded by the storm). Owner chose option A: a separate ABI reason for strict-parse drops. Witnesses added after the mutation check (PR #15).
ROADMAP item 9: the storm arithmetic moved to common::storm so that Kani proves it for every input (storm::proofs, calibrated by proof-task.py with three faults); the unit tests stay.

statement: The attack signal leaves out exactly the drops storm mode itself adds (strict-parse drops while storm adds STRICT_PARSE, fragment drops while it adds DROP_IPV4_FRAGMENTS) and nothing else: a malformed-header flood is an attack in every mode, so a storm cannot keep itself going on legitimate traffic.
